chapter_title: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha (PPARα) Agonists: A Potential Tool for a Healthy Aging Brain
source_pdf: /mnt/project-files/Experimental Provenance for QSAR Dataset/Pharmacology (Luca Gallelli) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).pdf

records.quote: tertiary prevention of AD dementia which refers to anticholinesterase drugs is known to modestly delay progression of dementia
records.notes: Class named without any compound. The book prints only 'anticholinesterase drugs'; the target name 'cholinesterase' and the role 'Inhibitor' are inferred from the prefix 'anti-', not stated as such.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.mechanism_book_wording: This receptor is activated by fatty acids and their derivates
records.quote: This receptor is activated by fatty acids and their derivates and among the synthetic ligands; by compounds of the fibrate family.
records.notes: The book contrasts these with 'synthetic ligands' but does not use the word endogenous or natural. Target class 'receptor' is stated on the page ('is a nuclear receptor'). 'Agonist' is the rule-name rendering of the book's 'activated by'.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.mechanism_book_wording: their mode of action is entirely via the activation of PPARα
records.quote: Fibrates are first-line drugs used for over 40 years to treat hypertriglyceridemia and their mode of action is entirely via the activation of PPARα.
records.numbers_given: clinical effect size (percent change in plasma lipids)
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 140: 'fibrates reduces plasma level of triglycerides by 30-50%, slightly increase HDL-cholesterol by up to 5-15 % and usually reduces LDL-cholesterol by 15 to 20%'
records.notes: Drug class, not a single compound. drug_kind 'approved drug' is inferred from the book's words 'first-line drugs used for over 40 years'. Page 148 words it as 'Fibrates act as synthetic ligands for PPARα'. Page 147 also says 'Fibrates are more selective to PPARα but they also have an action on PPARγ'; no direction is named there, so no separate PPARγ record was written for the class.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.quote: The impact of PPARα agonists on cognition was not deeply investigated at a large scale level but some observational studies are interesting.
records.notes: Mechanism named as a class without a compound. Page 135 is the chapter title. Page 142 has 'early treatment with PPARα agonist' (compound not named) and 'PPARα activators'. Page 148 has 'PPARα agonist' in body text and in the figure 8 caption.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.quote: Clofibric acid and fenobibric acid (active metabolites of clofibrate and fenofibrate) activate PPARα and PPARγ but they are 10 times more selective to PPARα.
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 141: '10 times more selective to PPARα' (versus PPARγ)
records.notes: The book describes it as the active metabolite of clofibrate.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Gamma Agonist
records.quote: Clofibric acid and fenobibric acid (active metabolites of clofibrate and fenofibrate) activate PPARα and PPARγ but they are 10 times more selective to PPARα.
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 141: '10 times more selective to PPARα' (versus PPARγ)
records.notes: The book describes it as the active metabolite of clofibrate. The expanded target name in the rule name is not printed for PPARγ in this chapter; it is built by analogy with the printed full name of PPARα.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.quote: Clofibric acid and fenobibric acid (active metabolites of clofibrate and fenofibrate) activate PPARα and PPARγ but they are 10 times more selective to PPARα.
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 141: '10 times more selective to PPARα' (versus PPARγ)
records.notes: Name kept exactly as printed, 'fenobibric acid' (probably a misprint of fenofibric acid; that reading is an inference). The book describes it as the active metabolite of fenofibrate.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Gamma Agonist
records.quote: Clofibric acid and fenobibric acid (active metabolites of clofibrate and fenofibrate) activate PPARα and PPARγ but they are 10 times more selective to PPARα.
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 141: '10 times more selective to PPARα' (versus PPARγ)
records.notes: Name kept exactly as printed, 'fenobibric acid' (probably a misprint of fenofibric acid; that reading is an inference). The expanded target name in the rule name is not printed for PPARγ in this chapter; it is built by analogy with the printed full name of PPARα.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.quote: Bezafibrate activates PPARα but can also be linked to PPARγ and PPARδ.
records.numbers_given: clinical effect size, treatment duration, plasma concentration of a metabolite (not potency data)
records.numbers_detail: PDF page 142: 'bezafibrate treatment for 12 weeks' ... 'postprandial insulin response 26% lower after bezafibrate'. PDF page 146: 'postprandial β-OHB response was 58% higher after bezafibrate treatment for 12 weeks' ... 'to reach 0.3-0.4 mM β-OHB at the end of the day'. PDF page 143, figure 4 caption: 'n=12, * p≤0.05'.
records.notes: drug_kind 'approved drug' is inferred from the book describing it as a second generation fibrate used in clinical trials; the book does not use the word approved. The same sentence says it 'can also be linked to PPARγ and PPARδ'; no direction is named, so no PPARγ or PPARδ record was written.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Alpha Agonist
records.quote: In rats treated with clofibrate, PPARα stimulation leads to an upregulation of MCT-1
records.notes: drug_kind 'approved drug' is inferred from page 141 ('a first generation fibrate and was used for numerous years'). Page 141 attributes PPAR activation to the active metabolite clofibric acid (separate records). 'Agonist' is the rule-name rendering of the book's 'stimulation'.

records.mechanism_rule_name: Peroxisome Proliferator Activated Receptor Gamma Agonist
records.quote: PPARγ stimulation is likely to be more effective than PPARα in inducing mitochondrial biogenesis
records.notes: Mechanism named without a compound. 'Agonist' is the rule-name rendering of the book's 'stimulation'; the book does not print the phrase 'PPARγ agonist' in the body text (it appears only in a reference title, which was not extracted). The expanded target name in the rule name is built by analogy with the printed full name of PPARα.

chapter_notes: Review chapter with no potency data (no IC50, Ki, EC50 or Kd); the only numbers are a '10 times' selectivity statement and clinical effect sizes. Not recorded because the page names no direct target or no direction: fenofibrate and gemfibrozil (named only as fibrates, page 141), fibrates 'action on PPARγ' (page 147), bezafibrate 'linked to PPARγ and PPARδ' (page 141), fibrate increasing transcription of HMG CoA synthase (page 145, gene expression), β-amyloid 'affecting' pyruvate dehydrogenase (pages 143-144), streptozotocine depleting brain insulin (page 142), and insulin acting at insulin receptors (pages 141-142, never stated as an agonist statement).
